title: One Gene, Many Questions
paragraphs: Autism is diagnosed less often in women and girls, and researchers have now pointed to a single gene on the X chromosome, ZFX, as a possible contributor to that gap. Females carry two X chromosomes and, unusually for X-linked genes, express both copies of ZFX, so they produce more of it than males do; the gene appears to keep other autism-associated genes switched on when they might otherwise be silenced. The widely quoted claim that autism is up to four times as common in males is contested, partly because autism presents differently in females and because many girls and women mask their traits, which delays diagnosis or prevents it altogether. Nevertheless, many specialists accept the existence of a female protective effect, and women who are diagnosed tend to carry more autism-linked mutations than diagnosed men, implying that females need a heavier genetic load before the condition becomes apparent.

To investigate, Rebecca Andersen's team grew neural progenitor cells in culture and used a gene-editing tool to degrade the RNA from 20 genes known to be linked to autism. Reducing any one of these genes usually lowered the activity of most of the others, a degree of convergence the researchers said they had not expected. A model of the interactions then identified a core of 70 genes that strongly regulate the 20 and one another, and, among genes more active in female brains, pointed to ZFX. If ZFX acts as a genetic buffer, a girl could inherit many variants that reduce the expression of autism-associated genes and yet be protected because ZFX raises it again. An independent expert called the idea biologically plausible, but cautioned that it rests on the model, that nobody has demonstrated that boosting ZFX rescues the effects of such variants, and that a protective effect this complex is unlikely to trace back to one gene alone.

options.text: A gene on the X chromosome may explain the lower diagnosis rate in females, since it is less active in them, which lets other autism-linked genes be silenced.
options.explanation: Kadınlar ZFX'ten erkeklerden daha fazla üretir; gen diğer genleri susturmaz, açık tutar.

options.text: A gene on the X chromosome may explain the lower diagnosis rate in females, since editing it in cultured cells showed that autism can be prevented.
options.explanation: Deneyler genlerin birbirine bağlı etkinliğini ve ZFX'i ortaya çıkardı; ZFX'i artırmanın otizmi önlediği hiçbir deneyde gösterilmemiştir.

options.text: A gene on the X chromosome may explain the lower diagnosis rate in females, since males who carry it are diagnosed only after years of masking.
options.explanation: Maskeleme ve gecikmiş tanı kadın ve kızlar için anlatılır; ZFX ile erkeklerdeki tanı süresi arasında böyle bir bağlantı yoktur.

questions.prompt: What does the finding that diagnosed women carry more autism-linked mutations than diagnosed men suggest?

options.text: Women may be more likely than men to inherit such mutations from their mothers rather than their fathers.
options.explanation: Mutasyonların kimden kalıtıldığı hakkında bilgi yoktur.

options.text: Such mutations may be less harmful to men than they are to women, whatever their number.
options.explanation: Bulgu, kadınlarda otizmin ortaya çıkması için daha fazla mutasyon gerektiğini ima eder; mutasyonların erkekler için daha az zararlı olduğunu değil.

options.text: Many men who carry such mutations may never be diagnosed, because autism goes unrecognised in them.
options.explanation: Mutasyon taşıyıp tanı almayan erkeklerden söz edilmez; tanı gecikmesi kadınlar için anlatılır.

options.text: Females may tolerate a greater number of such mutations before the condition becomes noticeable.
options.explanation: Tanı alan kadınların daha fazla mutasyon taşıması, kadınlarda otizmin belirginleşmesi için daha yüksek bir eşik gerektiğini düşündürür.
